answer: The crystal test starts from the attacker's ledger: a thousand fake agents should cost a thousand times one honest agent. A newcomer enters only when an established sponsor locks a bond behind it, and the bond is slashed if the newcomer is later proven fake. The cipher check ties the sponsor's own standing to every vouch, so backing a thousand clones needs a thousand sponsors willing to lose money and reputation. The marble does not need to catch every fake — it only needs to make faking more expensive than earning honestly.
